tasks.title: Encoding sweep + value-validating hygiene gate
tasks.objective: Every text-mode I/O boundary in factory/scripts names utf-8 explicitly per decision 0043's consumer classification, spawned Python children are contracted to UTF-8 via env, and the new AST-based check_encoding_hygiene gate (value-validating, allowlisted) reports zero violations - the machine-checkable definition of sweep completion.
acceptance_criteria: Subprocess captures classified by consumer: diagnostic captures (common.run_quiet - one change covering its ~15 doctor call sites - and human-facing prints) decode encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'; machine-consumed captures decode strictly - git path output keeps filesystem semantics (bytes or surrogateescape: stages path/digest authority, quickfix scope enforcement, pr_ready freshness paths), JSON protocol output (gh in project.py, merge-stage roadmap in roadmap.py) decodes strict utf-8 and fails loudly. Byte-mode sites (pr_ready.py:348, doctor.py:283, upgrade.py:159/314/324/355) untouched.

All ~100 text-mode file I/O sites name encoding='utf-8': read_text/write_text/text open()/Path.open (including JSONL appends in events.py/signal.py) - strict for evidence/plans/specs/manifests; errors='replace' ONLY at allowlisted human-display sites.

All six text temp-log handles (delegate.py:1055-1056, stages.py:855-856, stages.py:945-946) become encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' for the parent read-back, and each spawned child env sets PYTHONUTF8=1 (companion env in delegate, runner envs in stages) - a child does NOT inherit the parent handle's Python-level encoding, so the env is the contract; non-Python children degrade via replace.

stdin joins the sweep: factory_lib's hook JSON reader (~line 978) and the four record_*_from_json.py stdin paths read strict utf-8 (wrap sys.stdin.buffer with an explicit utf-8 TextIOWrapper or equivalent); a test pipes non-ASCII JSON through a recorder and asserts it round-trips.

NEW factory/scripts/check_encoding_hygiene.py: AST-based, VALUE-validating - flags (a) subprocess text captures whose encoding is absent or not literally 'utf-8', (b) read_text/write_text/text open()/Path.open (incl. append) without encoding='utf-8', (c) tempfile.TemporaryFile/NamedTemporaryFile text modes without it, (d) sys.stdin reads outside the blessed strict reader, (e) errors='replace' outside the allowlisted diagnostic sites. The allowlist carries the plan's DO-NOT byte-path list (Scope/Non-goals section, file:line) and documented exceptions; bytes-mode open and dir_fd idioms must not false-positive. Zero violations on the swept tree; self-tests prove it catches a seeded violation of each rule class and passes the allowlist.

The DO-NOT list is untouched: no errors='replace' on any digest-adjacent read (blocking review rule); existing nonconforming replacement reads (check_dual_runtime canon reads, upgrade's indexed-symlink read at :314-333) are reconciled to strict/lossless semantics or added to the documented exception list with a reason.

Decision 0043 text refined if implementation reveals corrections; status stays proposed. Full POSIX suite green under the pinned FACTORY_TEST_CMD. LESSON (repeated-full-file-rewrites-regress-prior-fixes): verify against committed HEAD after any multi-round rewrite; PR #101's landed reconfigure/run_cmd surface must survive byte-identical.

LESSON (fake-os.name tests / 3.11 pathlib dispatch): any new test faking platform state must not construct bare Path() under a patched os.name; prefer real-encoding subprocess probes (PYTHONIOENCODING / LC_ALL in a child process).

Review round (stage autoreview + orchestrator verification, 2026-08-13) — six fixes, one park: (1) RUNTIME BUG: check_dual_runtime's check_prototype_isolation now strict-decodes every tracked file, so any tracked binary (image/font/archive) raises UnicodeDecodeError and aborts the checker — read those files as BYTES (the scan only needs byte/marker semantics) or catch UnicodeDecodeError and skip binary content; add a test with a tracked binary. (2) RUNTIME BUG: read_stdin_utf8's temporary TextIOWrapper OWNS sys.stdin.buffer — when the wrapper is finalized it CLOSES the shared buffer, so any later stdin read in an embedding host hits I/O-on-closed-file. Read via the wrapper then call wrapper.detach() before it is discarded (or read raw bytes and decode explicitly); add a test that reads stdin twice in one process. (3) MISCLASSIFICATION: phase.py's git status --porcelain decode is PATH data — surrogateescape, not strict (plan AC1's filesystem class); fix and audit any other git path capture that got strict in the sweep. (4) GATE STRENGTH: the checker must reject any non-strict errors= policy (ignore, backslashreplace, a variable) outside the allowlisted diagnostic sites — not just the literal 'replace' — and the BYTE_PATH_ALLOWLIST must actually be consulted; wire it or delete it, dead allowlists lie. (5) GATE STRENGTH: subprocess TEXT INPUT is also locale-encoded — flag subprocess.run(..., input=..., text=True) and Popen(..., stdin=PIPE, text=True) without encoding, even when output is not captured. (6) GATE STRENGTH: the stdin rule must also catch input(), 'from sys import stdin' aliases, and getattr(sys,'stdin') forms — the shipped helper itself uses the getattr form and is invisible to the current rule; blessing happens via the allowlist, not via pattern blindness. PARKED: wiring check_encoding_hygiene into the CI workflow is ENC.2's task, not a gap in this stage. Selector for this round: hygiene self-tests + the new binary/stdin-twice tests + '-k encoding_hygiene or stdin or dual_runtime' green.

tasks.reviewer_focus: The DO-NOT list is the risky seam: any errors='replace' on a digest-adjacent or machine-consumed read is a blocking finding. Second seam: the child-env UTF-8 contract (PYTHONUTF8=1 in spawned envs) - the parent handle encoding alone is NOT the fix. Third: the hygiene gate must validate literal values, not keyword presence, or zero-violations is meaningless.

tasks.title: Locale-forced CI proof + docs
tasks.objective: CI proves the hardened flows under a genuinely non-UTF-8 locale on both platforms with runtime assertions that the forcing took effect, the Windows delegation E2E round-trips a non-cp1252 glyph through the worker handoff, and the docs/spec record the convention and story.
acceptance_criteria: check_encoding_hygiene.py joins the scaffold-check job's checker steps in factory-scaffold.yml (beside check_dual_runtime and the other standalone checkers) so the encoding convention is enforced on every PR, not just at stage close — the parked finding from ENC.1's review round.

factory-scaffold.yml gains an ubuntu step exporting LC_ALL=C and PYTHONUTF8=0 (explicit LC_ALL suppresses PEP 538 coercion; PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE not needed) that runs forge.py next, doctor --fast, and the four standalone checkers; the step first ASSERTS sys.flags.utf8_mode == 0 and a non-UTF-8 locale.getpreferredencoding(False) so a future coercion-rule change cannot false-green.

The windows-hook-gates job runs its selector with PYTHONUTF8 explicitly unset (real ANSI code page) and the same runtime assertion; the delegation E2E's success path has the fake companion emit a non-cp1252 glyph (e.g. U+2192) that must round-trip into the captured handoff without crashing the parent read-back.

docs/windows.md documents the encoding convention (0043) and the D-0026 parked scope; docs/specs/windows-zero-setup.md's Decomposition section gains story 5 (FORGE-WIN-ENC) - the grill-settled canon bookkeeping.
Every CI selector node id exists (D-0020); nt-only tests stay OUT of stage-local required_tests (WIN-3 lesson: stage done counts a skip as fail).

Existing init/adopt/upgrade propagation tests confirm the swept scripts and the new checker ship to vendored clients. Full POSIX suite green; windows-hook-gates green on the PR is the real proof - no pr_ready before it (WIN-2/WIN-3 lesson).

tasks.reviewer_focus: False-green is the enemy: both CI legs must assert the locale forcing actually took effect at runtime, and the Windows glyph round-trip must exercise the SUCCESS path, not just failure cleanup. Selector hygiene per D-0020.

tasks.title: Story-review fixes: gate blind spots + isolation-scan decode
tasks.objective: Three story-level autoreview findings land: the prototype-isolation scan catches non-UTF-8 sources again (replace-decode, allowlisted as diagnostic), and the hygiene gate learns io.TextIOWrapper and positional tempfile modes - closing the blind spots that would let the convention silently erode.
acceptance_criteria: check_dual_runtime's prototype-isolation scan must not SKIP undecodable tracked source - a non-UTF-8 source file (e.g. PEP 263 latin-1) could smuggle a prototype/ import past the gate. The scan is a diagnostic MATCHER: decode with encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' (ASCII marker matching survives replacement), and add that site to the hygiene allowlist as a documented diagnostic exception. Regression test: a tracked latin-1 file containing a prototype import is still caught.

check_encoding_hygiene validates io.TextIOWrapper constructions (missing or non-utf-8 encoding is a violation) - today removing encoding='utf-8' from read_stdin_utf8's wrapper stays green; seed-test the class.

tempfile.TemporaryFile/NamedTemporaryFile take mode as POSITIONAL ARG 0; the gate currently reads index 1, so TemporaryFile('w+t') without encoding passes - fix the index and seed-test the positional form.
check_encoding_hygiene exits 0 on the tree after the fixes; hygiene self-test selector green; no other files touched.
